# Assessment source restrictions — Debate 278

The controller reviewed all 2,446 canonical caption events. Assess the complete available recording, 5,759–5,877,080 ms. The supplied upload, organizer upload and archived audio all end after Tooley’s closing. A contemporary report also mentions Lennox’s closing, which could not be located. The user explicitly approved assessing this available recording with disclosure. Do not claim unabridged event coverage. Neither speaker may be penalized for missing material or replies; do not infer concession, evasion, absence of an argument or failure to answer from the missing closing. Do not reconstruct it from the report. The paid archive-tail transcription was only a completeness check, not a correction of canonical words or evidence for scoring a move.

## Motion and adopted burdens

The exact question is “Is Christianity more reasonable than atheism?”. Lennox defends Christianity; Tooley criticizes Christianity and defends atheism. This compares the cases made here; it does not assume those are the only possible worldviews or that rejecting Christianity establishes atheism. Tooley explicitly distinguishes his evidential objection to a perfectly good God from objections to particular Christian doctrines, allows an eternal God as a logical possibility, says science does not disprove God, and distinguishes atheism from materialism or denial of an afterlife. Preserve these distinctions. Lennox distinguishes scientific mechanism from agency and offers Christian accounts of reason, morality, hope and history. Judge each actual adopted claim rather than supplying a stronger argument from another work.

## Speaker and quotation ownership

The opening Lennox turn runs through event 201, followed by Tooley’s opening at 203–409. Thereafter named moderator handoffs, explicit first-person commitments and uninterrupted answers establish ownership. Audience questions begin around event 1718; primary-speaker answers begin at 1774. Moderator and audience premises are unscored context, not automatically claims adopted by either speaker. Brief mixed handoffs, laughter and interrupted attempted replies require conservative boundaries. Ideological fit alone is not attribution evidence. Mark materially unresolved ownership below high and explain the required audio check; never select high merely to avoid verification.

## Source qualifications to preserve

Tooley’s evil argument is evidential, not a claim of logical contradiction; his hypothetical limits on harmful power are not a demand to remove all choice. Lennox distinguishes sharing suffering and final justice from pretending to have a complete explanation of each tragedy. His hell reply refuses to assign Holocaust victims a known destiny and appeals to informed rejection; Tooley’s criticism must be assessed in its stated doctrinal scope. Lennox concedes that absence of an afterlife does not erase every humanly created meaning, while defending ultimate meaning. Tooley names and later sketches secular accounts of objective ethics; an appeal to a single atheist’s views is not automatically his own view.

When discussing evolution, Tooley explicitly limits special-creation objections to Christians who adopt that reading. His common-descent evidence includes chromosome fusion and noncoding DNA, not similarity alone. Lennox mentions an atheist critic of reductionism; that critic’s view is not itself an endorsement of Christianity. Lennox identifies his Rwanda testimony as indirect and anecdotal; Tooley admits he has not investigated possession carefully. Preserve those admissions. Both treat eternal ultimate reality as possible while disputing explanatory complexity. The moderator limits replies to several bundled questions; do not invent an opportunity for a complete answer or count an interrupted attempt as a completed argument.

These are source-fidelity constraints, not ratings, findings of success or failure, mandatory move selections, or reasons to avoid substantive criticism. Read the complete source independently.

## Caption caution and boundaries

Automatic captions contain recognizable corruptions of Tooley and Lennox, philosopher and book names, “deism,” “Higgs boson,” biblical references, and technical terms. Retain exact words in quotations; avoid corrupted passages as representative quotes. Do not treat apparent misspellings, wrong names, a numerical rendering or verse typography as a speaker’s error without verifying it. Early typhoon casualty numbers are spoken contemporaneous estimates; do not import later totals into this assessment. Repeated rolling-caption text and overlapping display times are preserved. Each source span must be the smallest contiguous passage that establishes the claim and supporting inference. Full-source review does not justify padding spans with unrelated claims.

The late closing invites wider comparative inquiry; reading recommendations are not proof of atheism. The available closing must be reviewed, but the unavailable Lennox closing creates no negative inference. No primary-speaker attribution audio check has been performed. The recorded archive-tail check confirms only the available edition’s ending.
